🧠 Crypto News Brief: Bitcoin opens Q4 stuck near $84K as stubborn bond yields cap a soft-inflation bounce. Wall Street keeps building — Citi turns bullish, Open USD goes live — but September's record hack losses show security still lags adoption. 📊 Bitcoin Starts Q4 Stuck in the $82K–$85K Range as Yields Cap PCE Bounce Bitcoin began the fourth quarter where it ended the third: boxed between $82,000 and $85,000. A softer-than-expected U.S. PCE inflation reading briefly lifted BTC above $85,000 and trimmed October rate-hike bets, but the move faded as long-dated Treasury yields stayed elevated, with the 30-year topping 5.6%. Spot bitcoin ETFs added pressure with $148.7M in net outflows on Sept. 30, ending a nine-session inflow streak, even though BTC closed Q3 up roughly 40%. Read full story 🏦 Citigroup Lifts 12-Month Bitcoin Target to $113,000 Citigroup raised its 12-month bitcoin forecast to $113,000 from $82,000 and its ether target to $3,028 from $2,240, according to a client note reported by Reuters. The bank expects about $5 billion of crypto inflows over the next year as advisers and brokerages gradually build allocations, pointing to returning ETF demand, a supportive macro backdrop and U.S. Treasury long-bond buybacks. The new BTC target sits roughly 35% above spot, yet still below the October 2025 record above $126,000. More details 💵 Open USD Stablecoin Goes Live With Stripe, Visa, Mastercard and Coinbase Open Standard's dollar stablecoin, Open USD (OUSD), is now live on Ethereum, Solana, Base and Tempo. It is issued by Stripe-owned Bridge, with reserves held at BlackRock, BNY and Lead Bank and monthly attestations promised, while founding partners Coinbase, Mastercard, Shopify, Stripe and Visa have committed more than $1 billion to seed supply. Businesses can mint and redeem 1:1 at no cost, with Coinbase access opening October 1 — a direct challenge to USDT and USDC. Steve Daines (R-Mont.) introduced the 56-page ADAPT Act, arriving two weeks after the House Ways and Means Committee advanced its own crypto tax bill 38–5. Adrian's DeFi Insights 

Автор: Adrian Pape


Автор: Adrian Pape

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/829k-decides-how-bitcoins-fourth-quarter-looks-adrian-pape-pix6e?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BceUgEj19RDGO0L2%2FJBG4AQ%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=2RCDQaQCslscs1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mupghcs9~bx-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mupghcs9-bx
  
Hey Friend! Two weeks ago I told you what I’d need to see to call the breakout: Two weekly closes above the 50-week moving average. Sunday delivered the second one. Bitcoin also closed September at $83.6k, its second green month in a row. The bond market didn’t get the memo though. The 30-year Treasury yield hit its highest level in 24 years on the same day Bitcoin ran to $85.3k. Even Ben Cowen, one of the most careful analysts out there, said this week that he didn’t expect Bitcoin above $83k. Nobody really knows what comes next, so this week I’ll show you the levels I work with instead of a forecast. My line is $82.9k, my add zone is $79.6k, and my cycle position keeps running with a liquidation price at $38k. ️ ⚡ On today's Episode: 📈 Macro Update – Core PCE came in at 3%, but mostly on paper after a revision. October hike odds fell to about 37%, the 30-year yield hit 5.65%, a 24-year high, and small caps are already down about 8%. 🔊 Crypto Pulse – Two weekly closes above the 50WMA at $77.7k, spot and futures demand still have to follow. 🐂 Alpha Insights – My cycle position runs at 1.64x with a liquidation price at $38k. $82.9k has to hold, $79.6k is my add zone, and $97.9k is the next big hurdle. The current state of the bigger market. Market Overview Start with inflation, because that’s what moved everything on Wednesday. Core PCE, the Fed’s preferred inflation measure, came in at 3.0% for August, lower than expected. Bitcoin jumped to $85.3k right after. Though most of that drop happened on paper. July was revised down from 3.3% to 3.0% too, after a change in how the number is calculated. So compared with last month, core inflation didn’t actually fall. The market still took it as good news. Two weeks after the Fed’s first hike since 2023, the odds of another hike at the end of October dropped to about 37%. The bond market doesn’t buy it. The 30-year Treasury yield hit 5.65%, its highest level in 24 years, and the 10-year reached 5.31%, the highest since 2002. One explanation for that: If the Fed pauses because inflation only looks lower on paper, bond investors worry that inflation keeps running, so they ask for higher yields. We can point to previous events like in 2018. The Fed hiked in September, skipped October, and the 10-year yield kept rising into early November before growth fears took over. For Bitcoin that patte
